77278.subject: Biology
77278.question_text: The Genus into which man is classified is
77278.explanation: In the biological classification (taxonomy) of humans, Homo is the correct genus. The full scientific name for modern humans is Homo sapiens, where Homo represents the genus and sapiens represents the specific species.

77279.subject: Biology
77279.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of the nymph of an insect. Study it and answer the question below:

The organism illustrated is a stage in the
77279.explanation:
Insects that have a nymph stage undergo incomplete metamorphosis (hemimetaboly), where the young look like smaller, wingless versions of the adult. Key examples include grasshoppers, cockroaches, termites, mantises, dragonflies, crickets, cicadas, and true bugs. 

In the illustration in question, that is the nymph stage of cockroach.

77280.subject: Biology
77280.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of the nymph of an insect. Study it and answer the question below:

The growth process that would occur in the organism before it becomes an adult is
77280.explanation: Moulting (also known as ecdysis) is the biological process by which a cockroach nymph sheds its rigid exoskeleton to allow its body to expand and grow. Because the exoskeleton is a hard outer shell that cannot stretch, the nymph must shed it periodically—typically between 5 and 13 times—to increase in size and eventually transition into a sexually mature adult.

77281.subject: Biology
77281.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of a dicot leaf. Study it and answer the question below.

The parts labelled I,II,III and IV respectively are
77281.explanation:
(See diagram above)

I - Apex

II - Midrib

III - lamina

IV - axil

77282.subject: Biology
77282.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of a dicot leaf. Study it and answer the question below.

The part that contains the phloem and xylem is labelled
77282.explanation: The midrib is the primary central vein of a leaf. It contains the vascular bundles, which are composed of xylem and phloem tissues. The xylem transports water and minerals from the roots to the leaf, while the phloem transports food (sugars) produced during photosynthesis to other parts of the plant.

77283.subject: Biology
77283.question_text: The functions of vacuoles in plants are storage and
77283.explanation: The central vacuole in plant cells plays a critical role in providing structural support through turgor pressure. When the vacuole is filled with water, it pushes against the cell wall, creating internal hydrostatic pressure that keeps the plant cell rigid and upright. This is why plants wilt when they are dehydrated and their vacuoles lose water.

77284.subject: Biology
77284.question_text:
Four cells each with osmotic potential of about 3% salt solution was immersed respectively into solutions of different concentrations as follows:

I - 1% salt solution; II - 3% salt solution; III - 6% salt solutuon; IV - 10% salt solution.

Which of the solutions will cause an increase in osmotic pressure within the cell?
77284.explanation: 1% salt solution will cause an increase in osmotic pressure within the cell because this solution has a lower salt concentration (1%) compared to the cell (3%). It is a hypotonic solution. Since water moves from areas of low solute concentration to high solute concentration via osmosis, water will enter the cell, increasing its internal volume and resulting in an increase in osmotic (turgor) pressure.

77285.subject: Biology
77285.question_text:
Four cells each with osmotic potential of about 3% salt solution was immersed respectively into solutions of different concentrations as follows:

I - 1% salt solution; II - 3% salt solution; III - 6% salt solutuon; IV - 10% salt solution.

If the cells are plant cells, what would happen to the cell in solution III? It would become
77285.explanation:
When a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution (6% salt solution vs 3% internal concentration), water leaves the cell via osmosis, causing the protoplast to shrink away from the cell wall. 

Solution I (1%): The cell is in a hypotonic solution; water enters, and it becomes turgid.

Solution II (3%): The cell is in an isotonic solution; there is no net movement of water, and the cell remains flaccid.

Solutions III & IV: The cell is in a hypertonic solution; water leaves, and it becomes plasmolyzed.

77286.subject: Biology
77286.question_text: How many molecules of oxygen are required for the aerobic respiration of three molecules of glucose?
77286.explanation:
A total of 18 molecules of oxygen (O\(_2\)) are required for the aerobic respiration of three molecules of glucose. According to the balanced equation for cellular respiration,  C\(_6\)H\(_{12}\)O\(_6\)  + 6O\(_2\)  →  6CO\(_2\)  +  6H\(_2\)O,

1 molecule of glucose requires 6 molecules of oxygen. Therefore, for three molecules of glucose, 3 x 6 = 18 molecules of oxygen are needed.

77287.subject: Biology
77287.explanation: Sclerenchyma is a simple permanent tissue in plants characterized by cells with heavily thickened, lignified secondary walls. Because these cells are usually dead at maturity and possess high rigidness, their primary role is to provide mechanical support, strength, and rigidity to plant organs.

77319.subject: Biology
77319.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of a cell carrying out a biological process. Study it and answer the question below:

The biological system that contains cells that carry out the illustrated biological processes in humans is
77319.explanation: The illustrated process typically refers to phagocytosis (a type of endocytosis), where a cell engulfs a solid particle, such as a bacterium. In humans, this biological process is primarily carried out by specialized white blood cells (phagocytes) which are integral components of the circulatory system as they travel through the bloodstream to identify and destroy pathogens.

77321.subject: Biology
77321.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct about respiration in plants?
77321.explanation: Respiration is a metabolic process that occurs in all living cells of a plant to generate energy (ATP). Unlike photosynthesis, it is a continuous process that happens both day and night and does not require light or the green pigment chlorophyll. Chlorophyll and light are specifically required for photosynthesis, which is the process of making food, whereas respiration is the process of breaking down that food to release energy.

options.text: It occurs in all plant tissues
Light and chlorophyll must be present for it to occur
Energy is produced as the end product
It occurs in the presence of oxygen

77324.subject: Biology
77324.question_text: Urine when compared with blood in mammals is hypertonic because
77324.explanation: Urine is considered hypertonic (more concentrated) relative to blood in mammals because the kidneys reabsorb a significant volume of water back into the bloodstream during the process of urine formation. This concentration occurs primarily in the Loop of Henle and the collecting ducts, where water is removed from the filtrate while solutes like urea and salts are retained. This mechanism allows mammals to conserve water and excrete waste efficiently.

options.text: urine contains high percentage of all cells
all traces of sugar have been removed from urine
urea is actively secreted into the renal tubules
much water has been removed from urine

77327.subject: Biology
77327.question_text: The naturally produced auxin in plants is
77327.explanation: The naturally produced auxin in plants is Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). It is the most common, abundant, and potent natural auxin found in vascular and lower plants. IAA is synthesized primarily in the apical meristems (growing tips) of stems and roots, young leaves, and developing seeds, typically from the amino acid tryptophan.

77331.subject: Biology
77331.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is responsible for the body's "fight-or-flight" response. Its primary role is to prepare the body for physical action or survival by mobilizing energy and redirecting blood flow to vital organs. The SNS triggers the release of norepinephrine, which binds to alpha-adrenergic receptors on vascular smooth muscle, causing vasoconstriction. This increases blood pressure and shunts blood away from the skin and digestive organs toward the heart, brain, and skeletal muscles.

options.text: increase in the secretion of saliva

77332.subject: Biology
77332.question_text: Long sightedness could be corrected using a
77332.explanation: Long-sightedness (hypermetropia) is corrected using a convex lens. These lenses are converging, meaning they bend light rays inward to focus them directly onto the retina, rather than behind it.

77336.subject: Biology
77336.question_text: During the process of hearing in mammals, the structure in the middle ear which receives the first vibration is the
77336.explanation: During the process of hearing in mammals, the malleus (also known as the hammer) is the first structure in the middle ear to receive vibrations.

77340.subject: Biology
77340.question_text: An important characteristics of fruits dispersed by water is the presence of
77340.explanation: Fruits and seeds dispersed by water typically possess a fibrous covering or husk. This adaptation is crucial because of buoyancy. The fibrous tissue traps air within its structure, which reduces the overall density of the fruit and allows it to float on water. Also,often combined with a waterproof outer layer, the fibrous husk protects the internal seed embryo from water infiltration and decay, especially in saltwater environments.

77343.subject: Biology
77343.question_text: Plants which grow and produce fruits within a year are called
77343.explanation: Plants which grow and produce fruits within a year are called annuals. These plants complete their entire life cycle—germination, growth, flowering, fruiting, and death—within one growing season or a single year. Examples include corn, watermelon, wheat, and rice.

77345.subject: Biology
77345.explanation: Chemical digestion in organisms is the breakdown of complex molecules into simple molecules.

options.text: breakdown of complex molecules into simple molecules
build up of simple insoluble molecules
build up of simple soluble molecules into complex insoluble molecules

77348.subject: Biology
77348.question_text: Excessive bleeding from an injury could be due to the lack of vitamin
77348.explanation: Excessive bleeding from an injury is primarily due to a deficiency of Vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting and stopping hemorrhage. A lack of this nutrient prevents the body from properly activating clotting factors.

77390.subject: Biology
77390.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of a cell carrying out a biological process. Study it and answer the question below:

The process is referred to as
77390.explanation: Phagocytosis, often called "cellular eating," is the specific type of endocytosis by which a cell uses its plasma membrane to surround and engulf large, solid substances. During this process, the cell extends arm-like projections called pseudopodia around the target particle, such as a bacterium.

77415.subject: Biology
77415.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of a system in humans. Study it and answer the question below.

Enzymatic digestion of protein begins in the part labelled
77415.explanation:
I - Stomach

II - Pancreas

III - Liver

IV - Gall bladder

Enzymatic (chemical) digestion of protein begins in the stomach - labelled part I. The stomach lining contains specialized cells called chief cells that secrete pepsinogen, an inactive proenzyme. When this comes into contact with hydrochloric acid (HCl) produced by parietal cells, it is converted into the active enzyme pepsin. Pepsin initiates the chemical breakdown of large protein molecules into smaller chains called polypeptides.

77430.subject: Biology
77430.question_text:
The diagram below is an illustration of a system in humans. Study it and answer the question below.

The parts that secret substances involved in the digestion of fats are labelled
77430.explanation:
I - Stomach

II - Pancreas

III - Liver

IV - Gall bladder

II - Pancreas: Secretes pancreatic lipase, the primary enzyme responsible for the chemical digestion of fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

III - Liver: Produces bile, a substance that emulsifies large fat globules into smaller droplets. This process increases the surface area of the fats, making it easier for enzymes to act on them.

While the gallbladder is involved in the process, it only stores and concentrates the bile produced by the liver; it does not secrete (produce) its own digestive substances.

77434.subject: Biology
77434.question_text: If the small intestine of an organism does not have villi, the organism will have a problem with
77434.explanation:
The villi are tiny, finger-like projections that line the inner walls of the small intestine. Their primary function is to maximize the surface area available for the final stage of nutrient uptake into the bloodstream. 

 If an organism lacks villi, nutrient absorption is severely impaired. The available surface area drops significantly, making it nearly impossible for the body to absorb essential sugars, amino acids, and fats efficiently.

options.text: digestion of food and absorption of nutrients

77446.subject: Biology
77446.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct about the dental formula of humans?
77446.explanation:
The correct dental formula for a permanent set of human teeth is 2:1:2:3 for each half of the jaw. This translates to 2 pairs of incisors, 1 pair of canines, 2 pairs of premolars, and 3 pairs of molars in each full jaw.

The correct answer is option C

options.text: One pair of canines is on the upper jaw and three pairs of premolars are on the lower jaw
Two pairs of incisors are the upper jaw and three pairs of premolars are on the lower jaw
Two pairs of incisors are on the upper jaw and three pairs of molars are on the lower jaw
One pair of canines is on the upper jaw and four pairs of molars are on the lower jaw

77449.subject: Biology
77449.question_text: The relationship between a bean plant and a Tridax plant on a farmland is
77449.explanation:
The relationship between a bean plant and a Tridax plant on farmland is competition because they are both autotrophic green plants that require the same limited resources to survive - sunlight, nutrients and space. 

In this interaction, neither plant benefits from the presence of the other; instead, the growth and yield of both may be reduced as they compete for these necessities.

77454.subject: Biology
77454.question_text: The following ecological factors affect all habitat except
77454.explanation: While temperature, light, and pressure are universal factors that affect both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, humidity refers specifically to the amount of water vapour in the air. Because aquatic habitats are fully submerged in water, humidity is not a relevant ecological factor for organisms living entirely within those water bodies.

77463.subject: Biology
77463.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of an ecological instrument used in a habitat. Study it and answer question below.

The ecological instrument is
77463.explanation: A Secchi disc is a simple, circular tool used to measure water transparency or turbidity in oceans, lakes, and ponds.

77490.subject: Biology
77490.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of an ecological instrument used in a habitat. Study it and answer question below.

The instrument is used to measure a factor
77490.explanation: The secchi disc is usually lowered into the water until it is no longer visible, while trying to measure water transparency or turbidity in oceans, lakes, and ponds.

77492.subject: Biology
77492.question_text: When Tilapias' population in a pond reaches the carrying capacity, the population
77492.explanation:
In ecology, when a population reaches its carrying capacity (K), it doesn't simply stop at a fixed number. Instead, it enters a phase of dynamic equilibrium. The population size typically oscillates (alternately increases and decreases) around the carrying capacity.

If the population exceeds K, resources like food and oxygen become scarce, leading to increased death rates or decreased birth rates, causing the population to decrease. Once it falls below K, resources become more available, allowing the population to increase again.

77493.subject: Biology
77493.question_text: Which of the following statements about the pyramid of energy is correct?
77493.explanation: An energy pyramid is a graphical representation of the flow of energy through different trophic levels in an ecosystem. It is always upright because energy is lost at each successive level. This loss occurs primarily through metabolic processes (such as respiration and movement) and as heat released into the environment. According to Lindeman’s 10% Law, only about 10% of the energy from one trophic level is transferred to the next, meaning energy content is highest at the base (producers) and lowest at the apex (top predators).

options.text: Energy remains constant across trophic levels
Energy decreases from the base to the apex of the pyramid
Energy increases from the base to the apex of the pyramid
each trophic level is an independent energy source

77496.subject: Biology
77496.question_text: Which of the following sequences represents the trend in eutrophication?
77496.explanation: Eutrophication is a process that occurs when a water body becomes overly enriched with nutrients (primarily nitrates and phosphates), often from agricultural runoff or sewage. This leads to the following sequential trend: Excessive nitrates → massive algal growth → lack of oxygen→ death of aquatic organisms.

options.text: Heavy mineralization→ lack of oxygen→ massive algal growth
Excessive nitrates→ massive algal growth →lack of oxygen→death of aquatic organisms
Excessive phosphates→lack of oxygen→massive algal growth→ death of aquatic organisms
massive algal growth→excessive nitrates→lack of oxygen

77499.subject: Biology
77499.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the term population? The number of
77499.explanation: The total number of a specific tilapia species living within a particular lake defines its population. In ecology, a population is defined as a group of individuals of the same species that are spatially separated (living in that specific lake) and interbreed.

options.text: fungus and snail on leaf litter
bees and butterflies on a flower
flatworms and roundworms in the gut of an animal.

77502.subject: Biology
77502.question_text: What is the population density of Ageratum sp. of frequency 1,850 on a land area measuring 100m\(^2\)?
77502.explanation:
Given:

Total number of individuals, N = 1,850

Total Area, A = 100 m\(^2\)

Population Density = \(\frac{Total individuals}{Total Area}\)

                               = \(\frac{1850}{100}\)

                               = 18.50 plants/m\(^2\)

77504.subject: Biology
77504.question_text: Which of the following activities does not control pathogens?
77504.explanation: While eating a balanced diet is essential for supporting a healthy immune system and improving your body's ability to resist infections, it does not directly target, eliminate, or control pathogens themselves in the way that physical or chemical interventions do.

77507.subject: Biology
77507.question_text: Which of the following diseases could be prevented by a BCG vaccination?
77507.explanation: The BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin) vaccine is specifically designed to provide protection against tuberculosis (TB). It is routinely administered at birth in countries with high TB prevalence.

77508.subject: Biology
77508.question_text: The main effect of a deforestation is
77508.explanation: Deforestation is a major contributor to soil erosion, biodiversity loss, and climate change. Trees act as anchors for the soil with their roots, and their canopy protects the ground from rain. When trees are removed, the soil is exposed to wind and rain, leading to severe erosion (loss of soil particles) and degradation. Deforestation destroys habitats, it does not create new ones.

options.text: reduction of carbon(IV) oxide in the atmosphere

77509.subject: Biology
77509.question_text: Which of the following resources cannot be conserved?
77509.explanation: Natural resource conservation is the planned management of resources to prevent exploitation, destruction, or neglect. Domestic wastes cannot be conserved because conservation applies specifically to natural assets that are useful or essential for survival. Instead, domestic wastes are managed through disposal, recycling, or reduction.

77510.subject: Biology
77510.question_text: Which of the following activities is not suitable for forest conservation?
77510.explanation: Felling of trees involves cutting down trees, which directly reduces forest cover and can lead to deforestation. Forest conservation focuses on protecting and managing forest resources to ensure their sustainability, making the widespread or unregulated removal of trees counterproductive to this goal.

77512.subject: Biology
77512.question_text: Which of the following pairs of features is an example of discontinuous variation?
77512.explanation:
Discontinuous variation (also known as discrete variation) refers to traits that fall into distinct, separate categories with no intermediate forms.

Fingerprints are categorized into specific, unique patterns (such as loops, whorls, or arches) and do not exist on a continuous spectrum.

Blood Groups of individuals belong to specific types (A, B, AB, or O) without any in-between values, making it a clear example of discrete categorization.

77513.subject: Biology
77513.question_text: The ability of some individuals to taste phenylthiocarbamide is
77513.explanation: The ability to taste phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) is a classic example of physiological variation because it relates to a difference in how the body functions or biochemical processes.

77514.subject: Biology
77514.explanation:
Specifically, alleles are variant forms of a gene located at the same position (genetic locus) on a chromosome within the cell nucleus.

Alleles reside on DNA, which is packaged into chromosomes. However, chromosomes (and therefore alleles) are located inside the nucleus of a cell.

77515.subject: Biology
77515.question_text: A couple heterozygous for albino genes have normal skin colour. What is the probability that their child would be an albino?
77515.explanation:
A couple heterozygous for albinism (both Aa), has a 1 in 4 (25% or 0.25) probability of having an albino child (aa). Because albinism is an autosomal recessive disorder, the child must inherit the recessive allele (a) from both parents to exhibit the condition. 

Key Genetic Probabilities:

  • 1/4 (25%) chance for an Albino Child (aa)
  • 2/4 (50%) chance for a Heterozygous Carrier (Normal) Child (Aa)
  • 1/4 (25%) chance for a Homozygous Normal Child (AA)

77516.subject: Biology
77516.question_text: The process occuring in the illustrated molecules above is
77516.explanation: DNA replication is the essential biological process of producing two identical replicas of DNA from one original DNA molecule, occurring in all living organisms prior to cell division.

77518.subject: Biology
77518.question_text: If the percentage of adenine in the DNA of a human is 32%, what would be the percentage of thymine?
77518.explanation:
If the percentage of adenine (A) in human DNA is 32%, the percentage of thymine (T) would also be 32%. 

This calculation is based on Chargaff's rules, which state that in a double-stranded DNA molecule, nitrogenous bases always pair in a specific manner:

  • Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T) (A = T).
  • Guanine (G) always pairs with Cytosine (C) (G = C)

77532.subject: Biology
77532.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct about colour blindness?
77532.explanation:
Both statements in options B and C are not correct based on the biological principles of sex-linked inheritance: 

Males cannot be carriers: Because colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait and males have only one X chromosome, they will always express the condition if they possess the gene. They cannot "carry" it without being affected.

Females can be carriers: Females have two X chromosomes. If they have the gene on only one of these chromosomes, they do not express the condition but can pass it to their offspring.

options.text: The trait is controlled by a recesive gene

77533.subject: Biology
77533.explanation: Lamarck's theory, also known as Lamarckism or the inheritance of acquired characteristics, posits that physical changes an organism undergoes during its lifetime—such as the development of an organ through increased use or its weakening through disuse—can be passed directly to its offspring. He famously used the example of giraffes stretching their necks to reach high leaves, suggesting this stretching resulted in longer necks that were then inherited by the next generation.

options.text: characteristics of organisms are not the sum of the characters of their parents
characteristics of organisms are determined by mutation
organisms transfer acquired characters to their offspring
organism acquire genes from their parents

77534.subject: Biology
77534.question_text: The castes of the organisms found in a beehive are
77534.explanation:
A honeybee colony is a complex social organization comprised of three distinct castes, each with a specific biological role: 

Queen: The single fertile female responsible for laying all the eggs in the hive.

Drones: Male bees whose sole biological purpose is to mate with a young queen to ensure genetic diversity.

Workers: Sterile females that make up the vast majority of the colony; they perform all manual labor, including foraging, cleaning, nursing larvae, and defending the hive.

77535.subject: Biology
77535.question_text: The theory of natural selection in evolution was formulated by
77535.explanation: The theory of natural selection was formulated by Charles Darwin, who independently reached the same conclusion.
